title: GPU Fragmentation, Compaction, and Admission Control Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This playbook describes detection, triage, automated mitigation, and long-term controls for GPU-side memory fragmentation and allocation inefficiencies that lead to sudden request admission failures or unexpected latency spikes. It defines a compact, production-safe compaction daemon design, integration points with the scheduler admission controller, telemetry and SLOs to monitor, and an incident response runbook for on-call engineers.

Problem statement

- Symptom: bursts of OOM/admission-rejects for otherwise-capable GPUs, high allocation retry counts, or elevated tail latency for model requests despite available aggregate free memory.
- Root cause class: fragmentation of device memory and inefficient allocation patterns (many short-lived small allocations, large pinned KV caches, transient CUDA allocations by third-party kernels) that leave free memory fragmented into non-contiguous regions. On some GPUs this prevents large contiguous allocations required by kernels or model KV caches and forces the runtime to fall back to slower execution paths or reject requests.

Why this matters

- Impact on SLOs: admission failures and long alloc-retry loops can increase p95/p99 latency and reduce throughput. Customers experience degraded responsiveness while dashboards report available_free_bytes but high allocation failures.
- Cost: noisy retries and degraded kernels increase per-token GPU time and therefore cost.

Key concepts and terminology

- fragmentation_score: heuristic ratio of unusable free regions over total free memory (0..1). Higher means worse fragmentation.
- compaction: coordinated evacuation of low-priority allocations and re-creation of large contiguous free blocks (software-level: free & reallocate or runtime-level: memory defragmentation APIs where available).
- admission control threshold: configured fragmentation_score and free_pct thresholds that gate new request acceptance.
- compactor_daemon: lightweight service bound to each node/GPU that performs safe compaction cycles and exposes a handshake with the scheduler.

Telemetry and signals to monitor (recommended PromQL / queries)

- metrics to emit from runtime and compactor:
  - runtime_gpu_free_bytes_total (gauge)
  - runtime_gpu_largest_free_block_bytes (gauge)
  - runtime_gpu_allocation_retries_total (counter)
  - runtime_gpu_fragmentation_score (gauge: 0..1)
  - compactor_cycles_total (counter)
  - compactor_last_duration_seconds (gauge)
  - admission_rejects_by_reason{reason} (counter)

- Example PromQLs:
  - fragmentation score (per-gpu): avg(runtime_gpu_fragmentation_score) by (gpu_id)
  - allocation-failure rate: increase(runtime_gpu_allocation_retries_total[5m]) / increase(runtime_requests_total[5m])
  - usable-free-pct: runtime_gpu_largest_free_block_bytes / total_gpu_memory_bytes

Acceptable thresholds (guidelines — tune per fleet)

| Metric | Warning | Critical | Rationale |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| runtime_gpu_fragmentation_score | >= 0.35 | >= 0.60 | Above 0.35 we see elevated allocation retries; 0.6+ correlates with admission rejects in historical traces |
| runtime_gpu_largest_free_block_bytes | <= 0.25 * total_gpu_memory | <= 0.15 * total_gpu_memory | When largest contiguous block < 25% of device, large KV caches or batching fails |
| allocation retries per 10k requests | > 50 | > 250 | Empirical thresholds from production baselines |

Detection rules and alerting recommendations

1. Fire a P1 if: average(runtime_gpu_fragmentation_score) >= 0.60 on >= 3 GPUs in a rack for > 10m and admission_rejects_by_reason{reason="fragmentation"} increases by > 50/min.
2. Fire a P2 if: per-GPU runtime_gpu_fragmentation_score between 0.35 and 0.60 sustained for > 30m or allocation retry rate > threshold.
3. Add a transient ticketed warning when usable-free-pct < 0.30 for any GPU host.

Runbook: immediate triage (on-call steps)

1. Confirm incident context
   - Check dashboards: fragmentation_score, largest_free_block, allocation_retries, admission_rejects.
   - Identify impacted models, GPU IDs, node names, and recent deploys.
2. Quarantine and redirect traffic
   - If admission_rejects are affecting production paths, update the routing policy to divert traffic off affected GPUs to a fallback pool (use priority fallback model variants).
   - Apply fast chroots: mark GPUs as DRAINING via scheduler API to prevent new requests while preserving in-flight ones.
3. Trigger a controlled compaction cycle
   - Use the compactor control endpoint (see CLI below) to request an immediate compaction on specific GPUs.
   - If compaction does not reduce fragmentation_score by > 30% within timeout, escalate to manual eviction sequence.
4. Eviction sequence (if compaction fails)
   - Evict low-priority sessions and persistent KV caches according to eviction policy: first global LRU small sessions, then candidate long-lived KV caches tagged as "evictable".
   - Re-check fragmentation metrics. If still degraded, schedule node restart as last resort.
5. Post-incident analysis
   - Correlate with recent kernel rollouts, third-party library changes, and model variants.
   - Create a regression/bug entry if compactor failed or if specific model access patterns consistently cause fragmentation.

Automated compaction design (summary)

- Goals: minimize user-visible impact, preserve in-flight sessions, avoid full node restarts, and provide deterministic improvements for fragmentation_score.
- Phases:
  1. negotiate: compactor queries scheduler for safe eviction candidates; marks epochs for short allocation quiesce.
  2. drain-small-allocs: pause/serialize new small non-critical allocations and attempt to free short-lived buffers.
  3. move-and-realloc: for evictable objects (large KV caches with copy-on-restore semantics), copy to host memory or alternate GPU then free and reallocate to coalesce free regions.
  4. resume: restore paused allocations and release scheduler drain marks.

Compactor safety knobs and config example (YAML)

```yaml
compactor:
  enabled: true
  run_interval_seconds: 300
  max_duration_seconds: 120
  safe_eviction_percentage: 0.20 # will not evict more than 20% of active sessions without manual approval
  min_fragmentation_delta: 0.25 # required improvement for auto-marking success
  telemetry_window_seconds: 60
  backoff_multiplier: 2.0
  per_gpu_parallelism: 1
  eviction_tags_priority: ["background-lru","low-priority-kv","test-sandbox"]
  admission_thresholds:
    fragmentation_score_warning: 0.35
    fragmentation_score_critical: 0.60
    largest_free_block_pct_warning: 0.25
    largest_free_block_pct_critical: 0.15
```

Scheduler admission control contract (API sketch)

- Input: request metadata (model_id, expected_peak_alloc_bytes, priority) and current GPU stats (free_bytes, largest_free_block_bytes, fragmentation_score).
- Decision logic (high level):
  - If fragmentation_score >= critical and expected_peak_alloc_bytes > largest_free_block_bytes * 0.9 => REJECT with reason=fragmentation.
  - If fragmentation_score >= warning and priority == low => DELAY / QUEUE with backoff token.
  - Otherwise ACCEPT.

CLI and control endpoints (examples)

- Trigger compaction for gpu-4 on node-22 with 10m timeout:

```bash
redwoodctl compactor run --node node-22 --gpu 4 --timeout 600
```

- Query per-GPU fragmentation scores over the last 15m:

```bash
redwoodctl metrics query 'avg_over_time(runtime_gpu_fragmentation_score[15m])' --gpu all
```

Integration testing and benchmarking guidance

- Synthetic benchmark: the benchmark must exercise mixed allocation patterns (many small allocations + occasional large KV loads). Use the synthetic mix generator in the perf-suite:
  - small_alloc_rate: 400/s, size_distribution: lognormal(mu=8, sigma=1.1)
  - large_kv_loads: every 30s load 8GB KV block
  - concurrency: 128 sessions per GPU
- Measure before/after compactor: fragmentation_score, p99 latency, allocation_retries, throughput.
- Expected improvements: successful compaction should reduce fragmentation_score by >= 0.3 and reduce allocation_retries by >= 60% in controlled benchmarks.

Long-term mitigations and engineering actions

- Kernel hygiene: minimize transient device allocations in commonly used kernels; reuse buffers; prefer pooled allocators. Instrument third-party libraries used by model runtimes.
- KV cache reshaping: provide API for proactively chunked KV cache placement that avoids huge single contiguous allocations when model variant supports sharded KV.
- Scheduler heuristics: gradually prefer GPUs with low fragmentation_score for large-batch or high-memory requests; prefer dense placement for small-session workloads to increase contiguous free spans elsewhere.

Rollout and canary checklist

1. Unit and integration tests for compactor logic with synthetic fragmentation scenarios.
2. Canary compactor enabled on 5% of nodes with telemetry reporting and auto-rollback. Monitor fragmentation_score and allocation_retries for 72 hours.
3. Enable admission control in passive mode (log-only) for two weeks. Verify alert signal fidelity.
4. Switch to active mode with conservative thresholds for an additional two weeks, verify customer SLOs.
5. Incrementally increase compactor aggressiveness and tune safe_eviction_percentage.

Post-incident review and RCA template

- Summary: one-paragraph incident description
- Timeline: 5–10 minute granularity events from detection to mitigation
- Detection root cause: instrumentation and signals that first indicated fragmentation
- Technical root cause: codepaths/kernels or workloads responsible for fragmentation
- Mitigation steps executed and effectiveness metrics
- Action items: short, medium, long-term (owners and deadlines)

Appendix: troubleshooting snippets and sample PromQL

- Find top 10 models contributing to allocation retries in the last 30m:

```
topk(10, sum by (model_id) (increase(runtime_model_allocation_retries_total[30m])))
```

- Compute per-node largest_free_block_pct:

```
runtime_gpu_largest_free_block_bytes / node_total_gpu_memory_bytes
```

- Example incident note to attach to postmortem:
  - "Compactor successfully reduced runtime_gpu_fragmentation_score from 0.68 -> 0.28 on node-42; admission rejects fell from 120/min to 2/min following controlled eviction of background caches. Root cause was a third-party kernel change that introduced ephemeral cudaMallocs without pooling."
